Definition: from G1537 and G3506; (by analogy) to slip off, i.e. quietly withdraw:--convey self away.
BiblicalUsage: Scripture uses ekneúō where we would say to slip away quietly. In John 5:13, the text says "for Jesus had conveyed himself away."
TheologicalSignificance: I take ekneúō as it stands: to slip away quietly.
RelatedEvents: The Healing at the Pool of Bethesda
